newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates cling to high levels.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates cling to high levels.

text.p: Dutch money market rates stuck to high levels in busy trade on Tuesday, with call changing hands between 3.25 and 3.31 percent.
Dealers said one to three month deposits had been well bid earlier in the session, but were quoted unchanged from Monday.
"With call regularly hitting 3.25 to 3.31 percent, you'd do better to buy one- or two-month deposits at the same price," one dealer said.
One-month deposits were quoted at 3.18/26 percent, and two- and three-month deposits at 3.20/28 percent.

Dealers said they had not seen any primary trade in Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs), but added some parties might be dealing directly with the Finance Ministry's Agency now that the Agency has increased the transparency of its DTC programme.

The Agency had raised its indicative prices for DTCs by one or two basis points, with paper maturing in July now set at 3.13 percent, DTCs maturing in August at 3.15 percent and those in December 3.20 percent.
"I guess they needed money. But there's still quite a gap with money market rates, so I don't think there's much being done," one dealer said.

Dealers said the rather high level of Dutch money market rates was likely to last a little longer, blaming this on the market's unfamiliarity with the central bank's new money market instruments introduced in May.
"Other than that, there are no fundamental reasons for these levels," one dealer said.
"You'd rather have too much than too little on your account (with the central bank), it's logical people are bidding each other up," another said.
Under the new money market policy, market players are no longer allowed to have a negative balance on their cash reserve account with the central bank at the end of the day.
Any such gap is automatically plugged at the central bank's marginal advance rate of 4.5 percent.
The guilder firmed fractionally against the mark, trading at 112.45 guilders per 100 marks versus 112.50 on Monday.
